answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a time-locked deposit before transacting, much like water forced through a narrow inlet: the channel admits one flow at a time, so flooding it with fake identities is prohibitively expensive. Attackers whisper cheap copies into existence, but each copy must lock capital that cannot move elsewhere. A glacier-like vesting schedule releases it gradually, so an attacker who abandons identities loses the deposit. Honest agents pay once and keep working; a sybil farm must pay hundreds of times, turning the attack into a losing trade.
